status: Adopted after root identity/alias review on 2026-10-28; wired into screening and versioned title discovery.
scope: 15 primary-source-verified discrete fragrance parents; existing scope/role/type/date guards remain mandatory. New parent production requires explicit aroma/flavor/fragrance intent.
shared_eligibility: Ingredient membership establishes a finite parent identity only. Papers must centrally administer/assay the unchanged parent for pharmacology/toxicology; centrally study aroma/perception; measure a permitted exact-parent physical property; or explicitly produce the parent for an aroma/flavor/fragrance purpose. Presence in a GC-MS list, breath biomarker panel, essential oil, generic synthetic substrate panel or drug-scaffold name is insufficient by itself. Composition studies require the separate validated composition-method route and do not become parent pharmacology.
shared_exclusions: No arbitrary derivatives, Schiff bases, complexes, substituted scaffold libraries, metabolites, polymer conjugates or compound families inherit membership.

No solvent/vehicle/reagent/stain/substrate-only records, incidental background/absence mentions, uncharacterized mixture assays, insect-only applications or environmental occurrence/removal engineering without an independently eligible central-parent endpoint.
Production must have explicit aroma/flavor/fragrance intent; generic drug intermediate or test-substrate synthesis is excluded.

Physical-property routes require the parent to be the measured/calculated target, not a solvent, modifier or auxiliary. Generic materials characterization and routine spectra alone are not the bounded physical-property route.
Short trade abbreviations and commercially ambiguous aldehyde C-number names are not unconditional exact aliases.
Retain stereochemistry, test purity and formulation; source membership of a generic identity does not prove a specific enantiomer has the same effects.
shared_status_caveat: Historical fragrance/flavor ingredient identity is distinct from current authorization, permitted concentration, safety and therapeutic efficacy. This research verifies membership and identity only, not unrestricted contemporary approval or safe use. No regulatory compliance or clinical conclusion is implied by FEMA, IFRA or FDA listing.

source_access_notes: The initial guessed FEMA benzylacetone URL was inaccessible; fragrance membership instead rests on the official IFRA CAS row plus accessible NIST saturated-parent identity. No membership claim is taken from suppliers.
Several guessed anisaldehyde URLs were inaccessible; the explicit FEMA p-methoxybenzaldehyde record was accessible and matches IFRA CAS 123-11-5.

Some direct NIST URLs were inaccessible through browsing; only accessible NIST/FDA records and inspected FEMA/IFRA contents support the retained aliases. Para/4-methoxy equivalence and orthographic forms are normalized chemical nomenclature, not guessed trade formulations.
review_and_adoption_requirements: This proposal does not activate any parent or alias.
Review all identity/role guards before any later adoption; lexical name hits alone cannot establish an unchanged parent.

Alias matching must resolve the longest complete parent identity and apply derivative context guards: ethyl vanillin must not be attributed to unchanged vanillin, ester names must not be attributed to their precursor alcohol/acid, and benzylacetone must not be conflated with benzylideneacetone or phenylacetone.
Source rows establish fragrance identity; literature usefulness remains unquantified and must not be reported as additional papers.
Only this proposal file was written. Active allowlists, pipeline, database and Site were not edited; no collectors ran.

The file is prepared for review and is not referenced by pipeline code in this change.
All 15 identities have individual CAS/name rows in the official IFRA fragrance glossary. Ingredient membership is independent of current regulatory authorization or safe use.
